text: The Tavrin Valley’s sugar beet crop failed this season, according to a harvest bulletin released on Tuesday by the valley’s agronomy office and reviewed by The Continental Record. The document said prolonged spring flooding, followed by a six-week dry spell, cut expected yields by 68 percent and left much of the 14,200-hectare planting unharvestable. Chief agronomist Mira Vels told the paper that root rot spread rapidly in low-lying fields near Loden Marsh, while late frost damaged younger stands in the east basin. The bulletin estimated direct losses at 41.3 million thalers and said processors in Bracken Port would run below capacity through November. Local officials are preparing emergency feed imports to offset the shortfall.
